answer: Resist Sybil attacks with a capped vouching graph. Each established agent may sponsor only a few newcomers, and every sponsorship locks a bond, slashed if the newcomer misbehaves. A newcomer starts with almost no privileges; trust grows by a delta each epoch only while independent peers attest its work. Forging one fake identity is cheap, but forging a hundred needs a hundred sponsors risking real funds and honest histories. The pearl is that trust is earned slowly and lost instantly, while onyx-hard slashing makes mass fakery unprofitable: every identity costs a bond and epochs of waiting.
